etymology: From the advice attributed to Steve Bannon: drown the press in so much material that nothing can be checked.
trigger: A story that has to be survived rather than answered, and a press corps with finite hours.
tell: Eleven announcements in one afternoon, three of them real, and a briefing that outruns the fact-checkers by design.
counter: Pick one thread and pull it to the end. A flood is only a defence if the other side tries to drink all of it.

confused_with.tell: The slopagandist fills the feed with volume for money; flooding the zone fills it with volume for cover.

senses: The move of releasing more than anyone can process: real stories, fake stories and irrelevant stories in the same hour, so the true ones cannot be separated in time to matter.

It works because verification is slower than publication. Each item costs the press minutes to check and the source seconds to produce, and that asymmetry is the whole tactic - the flood does not have to convince anybody, only to keep them busy.
example: *"Nine press releases before noon, two of them true, and **flood the zone** worked exactly as designed: by Friday the story was a list nobody had finished."*
